title: EU AI Act Article 64 — EU Database Registration for High-Risk AI Systems: Obligations and Timeline
context: 2026-08-28 engine cycle — EU AI Act high-risk obligations phase; Article 64 mandates a publicly accessible EU database for high-risk AI systems; providers and deployers must register before placing on market (Aug 2026 enforcement commencement)
body: EU AI Act Article 64 establishes a mandatory, publicly accessible EU database for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III. From the August 2026 enforcement commencement date, providers must register each high-risk AI system — including its intended purpose, risk management documentation, conformity assessment results, and post-market monitoring plan — BEFORE placing it on the EU market or putting it into service. Deployers of high-risk systems (public bodies and certain private operators) must also register their use. This is not a voluntary transparency register: it is a legally binding pre-market obligation enforceable by Member State market surveillance authorities under Article 65. For a verification-first operator, the Article 64 database is a structural transparency instrument: every registered system carries a unique EU identification number that becomes a natural anchor for a verified measurement credential. The Council of AI maps Article 64 registration fields to its benchmark card schema so that conformance evidence — model safety scores, bias audit results, robustness test outcomes — is independently verifiable rather than self-declared. The posture is monitored containment, not provable isolation: registration proves the system is on the public record under regulatory oversight, not that it is safe. The verification credential closes the gap between registration and trust.
